title: Sales Demo Scenario Checklist (SE pre-flight)
content:
Purpose
This is the SE pre-flight checklist for the Redwood demo tenant. Goal: reduce “live demo surprises” (429s, auth/RBAC, model availability/pins, empty dashboards, fallback not triggering, etc.) and ensure the scenario runner + Console tour are ready.

Use this for:
- Standard 30-min demo (API + economics + reliability + Console)
- Short 20-min exec demo (API + 2 proof points)
- Enterprise/security add-on (narrative + screenshots)

Owner on point during demo: SE running the demo. Escalation: #demo-oncall (primary), #eng-sre (if infra), #eng-platform (Console/seed/ingestion).


A) T-60 to T-30 minutes: Environment selection + access sanity
[ ] Confirm which demo variant you’re running:
    - Hosted-first (default)
    - Dedicated-capacity talk track (focus on throughput predictability, isolation)
    - Private/VPC narrative add-on (screenshots/architecture)

[ ] Confirm you’re in the correct org/tenant:
    - Org name must include “DEMO” (never use anything resembling a customer org)
    - If you’re unsure, stop and ask in #demo-oncall

[ ] Confirm you have the right user role:
    - Console access: Demo SE role (RBAC)
    - Ability to view Usage/Latency dashboards and Rollouts view

[ ] Confirm you have the right API key for today’s demo:
    - Use a scoped “demo-runner” key (least privilege)
    - Verify key is not expired (if short-lived)
    - Verify key is not copied into a customer email or pasted into non-approved docs

[ ] If this is a screenshared demo:
    - Close any non-demo Console tabs, Slack DMs, and internal dashboards
    - Turn off browser autofill overlays
    - Have backup screenshots open (but not visible) in a second desktop

Notes to self (customer context / what to emphasize):
- ICP:
- Primary pain (latency/cost/reliability/security):
- “Must show” module(s):


B) T-30 to T-20 minutes: One-command healthcheck (must be green)
Run the demo healthcheck and read the output top-to-bottom. Do not start the live demo if any “red” items.

[ ] Run:
    redwood demo healthcheck --tenant demo --format summary

Expected PASS checks:
[ ] Auth: key valid, scopes OK for (chat, embeddings if needed, console read)
[ ] Quotas: requests/min + tokens/min sufficient for expected concurrency
[ ] Capacity: demo pool available in the region you’ll use
[ ] Model pins: pinned demo models resolvable and “READY”
[ ] Fallback policy: enabled on demo routes and compatible variants present
[ ] Telemetry ingestion: Console pipelines healthy (no backlog warnings)

If FAIL:
- Quota/capacity: see “Capacity & quotas runbook” + ping #demo-oncall with the healthcheck output pasted
- Auth/RBAC: ping Ethan Park / #eng-platform (include org id + your user email)
- Model pin/fallback: ping Mina Haddad or Ravi Menon (include route name + region)


C) T-20 to T-10 minutes: Seed data + scenario prerequisites
Console should look “lived in” but all data must be synthetic.

[ ] Confirm seeded objects exist (in the demo project you’ll use):
    - Routes (chat, structured output, tool-calling, embeddings/rerank if using)
    - Prompt sets / eval set (if showing quality regression / rollouts)
    - Rollout artifact (at least 1 canary/A-B entry visible)

[ ] Confirm naming conventions look clean on screen:
    - Route names are demo-friendly (no internal-only codenames)
    - Project names reflect “Demo - <Scenario> - Slot <#>” if doing parallel demos

[ ] Confirm time range defaults won’t show empty graphs:
    - Switch Console dashboards to “Last 60 minutes” (or “Last 24 hours” if needed)
    - Pre-select the correct project/route filters

[ ] If dashboards look sparse/empty, generate traffic now (do NOT wait until the call):
    - Start synthetic traffic job preset:
      redwood demo traffic --preset standard --duration 8m
    - Wait 2–3 minutes and refresh Console graphs

[ ] Confirm that error analysis is safe to show:
    - No raw prompt content that looks customer-specific
    - No links to internal-only systems in visible UI sections


D) T-10 to T-5 minutes: Live API sanity (fast smoke tests)
Run 3 quick API calls from the demo app or CLI.

1) Streaming chat completion
[ ] Run streaming request (demo app “Scenario 1: streaming”) and confirm:
    - Tokens stream smoothly (no frequent reconnects)
    - Latency feels “snappy” (subjective, but no obvious stalls)

2) Structured output
[ ] Run structured output scenario and confirm:
    - Output validates against schema
    - Retry behavior doesn’t loop or hang

3) Tool calling
[ ] Run tool calling scenario and confirm:
    - Tool invocation occurs
    - Tool result is incorporated
    - No auth failures to tool endpoint (if mock tool is used)

If anything fails:
- Switch region (if part of the script) OR switch to backup mode.
- Do not live-debug in front of customer beyond 30–60 seconds.


E) T-5 minutes: Reliability / fallback routing check (quick + visible)
We need confidence that fallback will behave as narrated.

[ ] Confirm the “primary” route model is pinned (visible in route config / rollout view).
[ ] Trigger a controlled fallback test (only in demo project):
    - Use the demo runner’s “Fallback test” button OR CLI:
      redwood demo fallback-test --route <demo-route> --region <your-region>

Expected:
[ ] Request succeeds
[ ] Response metadata indicates fallback variant used (model family/region) OR the Console routing panel shows the fallback event
[ ] The narrative matches reality: “We degrade gracefully to a compatible variant/region to keep the app up.”

If fallback test doesn’t trigger:
- Don’t mention fallback in the main arc; keep it as “optional module” and use screenshot/recording.
- Notify #demo-oncall with route + region.


F) Parallel demos hygiene (if you’re not the only SE running today)
[ ] Confirm you have an isolated slot:
    - Separate project (preferred)
    - Separate API key
    - Separate synthetic traffic namespace/preset if applicable

[ ] Double-check you’re not about to reset someone else’s slot:
    - If you need a reset, use the slot-specific reset command only


G) Backup mode readiness (must always be available)
If any of these are true, plan to use backup mode for that section:
- You see intermittent 429s
- Streaming disconnects
- Console graphs aren’t populating consistently
- Rollouts page is slow/flaky

Backup assets to have ready BEFORE the call (in a separate tab/window):
[ ] Annotated Console screenshots (economics dashboard, traces/error analysis, rollout view)
[ ] “Known-good” outputs for structured output + tool calling
[ ] Short recording of fallback routing event (if available)


H) Final 60-second pre-join check
[ ] Browser updated/restarted recently (avoid last-minute browser instability)
[ ] Demo app server is running locally (or hosted) and you’ve refreshed once
[ ] Console logged in to correct org/project with correct time range
[ ] API key loaded into demo app environment
[ ] You have the run-of-show open with timestamps + handoff cues


Post-demo (quick reminders)
- If you hit any demo issues (even if you recovered), log it:
  - Add a note to the demo QA tracker + paste the relevant error/output
  - If it’s a true failure mode (quota/auth/model/Console), open a ticket or ping #demo-oncall
- If you used backup mode, note why (to prioritize fixes)

Changelog
- 2026-02-10 (Markus): Added explicit fallback-test step + clarified time-range defaults for Console dashboards.
- 2026-01-23 (Sean): Updated escalation guidance and “no live-debug > 60s” rule of thumb.
- 2025-12-03 (Simran): Added parallel-demo slot hygiene section.
